The problem asks to generate a graph with 14 vertices where the maximum clique size is at most 3, the chromatic number is at most 5, and every vertex has degree at least 5.
I need to create a graph with 14 vertices that has no clique larger than 3, can be colored with at most 5 colors, and every vertex has at least 5 neighbors.

To construct it, I start with a graph that's almost complete but remove edges to avoid large cliques, but that might not 5. Instead, I think of bipartite graphs since they have small chromatic number and no large cliques.

A complete bipartite graph K_{5,9} has 14 vertices, split into parts of 5 and 9. Every vertex in the smaller part connects to all 9 in the larger, so degree  9, and those in the larger connect to all 5, so degree 5. Perfect, min degree 5.

Since it's bipartite, chromatic number is 2, which is less than 5, and the largest clique is just 2, since no triangles.

So this works.

Now, to list the edges. Vertices 0-4 in one part, 5-13 in the other. Edges between them only.

The edges are all (i,j) with i in 0-4, j in 5-13.

To present as a list of edges with u < v, yes, since 0-4 < 5-13.

So the list is (0,5),(0,6),...,(0,13), (1,5),...,(1,13), and so on up to (4,5) to (4,13).
